$comment: GENERATED by scf-core/scripts/build_negative.mjs. The negative fixtures of spec/conformance.md §5.3. Each case: start from an empty conforming database (spec/scf-schema.sql, plus the header stamps and _scf_meta.schema_version of §1.2), apply `statements` in order, then validate. A statement ending `-- params: [...]` binds that JSON array to its `?` placeholders. Compare against the case's <name>.expected.json as conformance.md §6.1 says: each finding's code, severity, table, count and rowIds; message, title and spec are for people.

cases.name: uuid-missing
cases.about: A row with no uuid. Nothing can track it across a file.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('INT. VOID', NULL)

cases.name: uuid-duplicate
cases.about: Two rows sharing a uuid. Lineage becomes ambiguous.
statements: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_scene_uuid
INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('A', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('B', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: uuid-malformed
cases.about: A uuid that is not uuid-shaped.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('C', 'not-a-uuid')

cases.name: relationship-endpoint-absent
cases.about: A relationship pointing at a character that is not here.
statements: INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('ELEANOR', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 404, 'mutual', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

cases.name: relationship-contradictory
cases.about: One pair described as both mutual and directed. No tool can pick the winner — the case §6.5's directionality flag exists for.
statements: INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('ELEANOR', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('MARCUS', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 2, 'mutual', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 2, 'a_to_b', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"]

cases.name: relationship-directionality-absent
cases.about: A relationship with no symmetry fact. Readable, but nothing can tell a duplicate from a second direction. Note the explicit NULL: the column defaults to 'mutual', so this state is only reachable by clearing it — which is exactly what an import from a tool that has no such concept would do.
statements: INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('ELEANOR', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('MARCUS', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 2, NULL, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]

cases.name: span-boundary-dangling
cases.about: An act anchored to a scene that is not present. Structure must still derive (§5.5) and say so.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. KITCHEN', '1', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO act (name, act_number, start_scene_id, uuid) VALUES ('Act I', 1, 999, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

cases.name: span-boundary-cut
cases.about: An act whose start scene is cut. A cut scene takes part in no span (§6.6.1), so Act II covers nothing and its scene stays in Act I (§5.5); the boundary is still there, so this is not `structure.boundary_dangling`, and without its own code the re-parenting would be silent.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. KITCHEN', '1', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, lifecycle_status, uuid) VALUES ('EXT. RIDGE', '2', 'cut', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. CHURCH', '3', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]
INSERT INTO act (name, act_number, start_scene_id, uuid) VALUES ('Act I', 1, 1, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"]
INSERT INTO act (name, act_number, start_scene_id, uuid) VALUES ('Act II', 2, 2, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005"]

cases.name: junction-key-null
cases.about: Two motif appearances on a prop, at no scene. Their natural keys (§6.3) agree except that `scene_id` and `domain` are NULL in both, and NULL key columns compare EQUAL (§6.4): one link, written twice. A reader comparing with SQL's `=` sees two distinct links and reports nothing.

INSERT INTO prop (name, uuid) VALUES ('Locket', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

INSERT INTO motif_appearance (motif_id, scene_id, entity_type, entity_id, uuid) VALUES (1, NULL, 'prop', 1, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"]

cases.name: asset-escapes-root
cases.about: An identifier containing '..'. It cannot be resolved, and a resolver that followed it would leave the project.
statements: INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["escape","@project/../../etc/passwd","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: asset-absolute
cases.about: An absolute identifier. Representable on purpose (§8.2), non-portable, and a warning rather than an error.
statements: INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["plate","/Volumes/plates/sh010.exr","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: unknown-table
cases.about: A table SCF does not define. Preserved and ignored (§10.1) — reported at info, because unknown usually means historical.
statements: CREATE TABLE legacy_pipeline (k TEXT, v TEXT)
INSERT INTO legacy_pipeline (k, v) VALUES ('shotgun_id', 'sg-1')

cases.name: line-type-unknown
cases.about: A screenplay line typed `scene_heading`, which is not in §1.3.1's closed set. A reader must keep it as unknown content and must not read it as a heading, so story order would silently lose a scene; an error, because two readers that disagree here disagree about the story.
statements: INSERT INTO screenplay_lines (line_order, line_type, content, uuid) VALUES (1, 'scene_heading', 'INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: junction-endpoint-absent
cases.about: A cast link with no character. A link with a missing end connects nothing; the row is kept and reported (§9.1), as `junction.endpoint_absent` rather than `field.required_absent`, because what is missing is half of a relationship.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. KITCHEN', '1', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO scene_character (scene_id, character_id, uuid) VALUES (1, NULL, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

cases.name: reference-dangling
cases.about: Three references that are filled and name no row: an ordinary one (a cast link to character 404), a polymorphic one (a thematic connection to character 404, found through its `entity_type` sibling, §12.1.2), and a uuid stored as text in an integer reference column, which is what a writer that skips the uuid-to-row-id step leaves behind. Each is `reference.dangling` (§9.1): one finding per column. None is `junction.endpoint_absent`, because the column is not empty; every query still answers (§9.2), and the link is not there.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. KITCHEN', '1', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO scene_character (scene_id, character_id, uuid) VALUES (1, 404, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO theme (name, uuid) VALUES ('Guilt', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]
INSERT INTO thematic_connection (theme_id, entity_type, entity_id, uuid) VALUES (1, 'character', 404, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"]
INSERT INTO motif (name, modality, uuid) VALUES ('The locket', 'visual', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005"]
INSERT INTO motif_appearance (motif_id, entity_type, entity_id, uuid) VALUES (1, 'scene', ?, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006"]

cases.name: asset-orphans-two
cases.about: Two assets nothing references. One condition on one table is one finding (§9.5): `asset.orphan` once, with `count` 2 and both rows in `rowIds` — not two findings, and not one row.
statements: INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["plate_a.exr","@project/plate_a.exr","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["plate_b.exr","@project/plate_b.exr","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

cases.name: section-mismatch
cases.about: A section line bound to an act whose record has since been renamed. The record answers queries and the line is the authoring handle (§1.3.1), so this is info: between commits the two may differ, and a line that has drifted is how an editor renames the wrong act.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. KITCHEN', '1', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO act (name, act_number, start_scene_id, uuid) VALUES ('The Thaw', 1, 1, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

INSERT INTO screenplay_lines (line_order, line_type, content, metadata, uuid) VALUES (1, 'section', '# The Arrival', ?, ?)   -- params: ["{\"structureRef\":{\"kind\":\"act\",\"uuid\":\"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002\"}}","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]
INSERT INTO screenplay_lines (line_order, line_type, content, scene_id, uuid) VALUES (2, 'heading', 'INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT', 1, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"]

cases.name: bundle-unbound
cases.about: A bundle with an asset in it and no binding anywhere. Its asset is referenced, so §8.6's orphan finding stays silent, and the cascade starts at a subject and never arrives — nothing resolves it at any position. Info: assembling a bundle before deciding what it is for is an ordinary state of an unfinished film.
statements: INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["kitchen plate","@project/plates/kitchen.exr","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO bundle (name, intent, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["Kitchen plates","visual_identity","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO bundle_asset (bundle_id, asset_id, uuid) VALUES (1, 1, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]

cases.name: header-unstamped
cases.about: No application id. Every file written before schema 2.10 looks like this, and a reader MUST NOT refuse it (§1.2).
statements: PRAGMA application_id = 0
PRAGMA user_version = 0
